findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — P1 C100: `return response;` — The helper returns a Fetch `Response` on the sync path but arbitrary provider-specific parsed objects/Gaxios responses on the fallback path, so callers cannot uphold one response contract and Google and HubSpot dereference nonexistent fields when credential sharing is enabled.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — P1 C100: `data: { key },` — `key` is the entire Zod `SafeParseReturnType` returned by `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, so a successful refresh persists `{ success, data }` instead of the credential payload and the next service construction cannot parse the stored credential.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — P1 C100: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number(),` — Converting Zod schemas to computed property-name strings does not define catch-all numeric/unknown fields, so the sharing-mode parser strips expiry metadata and Office 365 retains an already-expired timestamp that forces a refresh on every request.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — P1 C100: `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token";` — Replacing an absent refresh token with a magic placeholder changes “not supplied” into an apparently valid credential, causing later refresh attempts to send the literal placeholder instead of preserving the prior rotating token or representing absence explicitly.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:106 — P1 C100: `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token,` — The method fetches and persists a new access token but constructs the live Salesforce connection from the stale pre-refresh credential, so the operation that triggered refresh still authenticates with the expired token.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — P1 C75: `const appCredential = await prisma.credential.findFirst({` — The check-then-create sequence has no transaction or uniqueness-backed upsert, so concurrent sync deliveries can create duplicate user/app credentials and downstream `findFirst` readers can select an arbitrary version.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — P1 C75: `const response = await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, {` — The shared credential-sync dependency is invoked without an abort timeout, retry budget, or fallback, allowing one stalled endpoint to pin every expired-token calendar/video operation and exhaust shared request capacity.

packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:93 — P1 C100: `key: responseBody as unknown as Prisma.InputJsonValue,` — The sync endpoint is documented to return only an access token and expiry, yet this adapter replaces the whole credential with that partial response and therefore loses the refresh token and email required after the service is reconstructed.

docs/tasks/task-001.md:2 — P1 C100: `Review the change.` — The task defines no acceptance criteria for credential synchronization, provider coverage, error behavior, or success conditions, so there is no traceable basis for declaring the implementation complete.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — P1 C100: `export default async function handler(req: NextApiRequest, res: NextApiResponse) {` — The new externally reachable credential create/update workflow has no accompanying verification for its authorization rejection, malformed body/ciphertext, missing user/app, create, and update paths, leaving its core contract unvalidated.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 — P1 C100: `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId) {` — The new shared-vs-provider refresh branching has no accompanying verification of enabled, disabled, team-owned, remote-error, and provider-specific response paths despite changing token refresh behavior across six integrations.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — P1 C100: `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` — The sync branch returns a standard Fetch `Response`, which has no `data` property, so every enabled Google credential refresh dereferences `undefined` and cannot complete.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — P1 C100: `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` — When sync is enabled this helper returns an unparsed Fetch `Response`, not a `HubspotToken`, so `expiresIn` and `accessToken` are unavailable and the refreshed credential is unusable.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — P1 C100: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number(), ... [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional(),` — Both computed keys stringify to the same literal `"[object Object]"`, so this is not a valid Zod catch-all/expiry declaration and the schema strips the expiry fields the sync response is required to provide.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — P1 C100: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); ... data: { key },` — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns Zod's `{ success, data }` result envelope rather than parsed credential data, so Google persists the envelope as its credential key and subsequent consumers cannot find token fields at the expected top level.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101 — P1 C100: `return new jsforce.Connection({ ... instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url, accessToken: credentialKey.access_token, refreshToken: credentialKey.refresh_token, });` — The method fetches and stores a replacement access token first but then constructs the live connection from the stale pre-refresh credential, so the newly added refresh step cannot make Salesforce authentication succeed.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — P1 C100: `if (req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET)` — When `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset, a request with the header omitted compares `undefined` to `undefined` and bypasses authentication, allowing arbitrary users' stored OAuth credentials to be overwritten.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — P1 C75: `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` — Falling back to a public empty encryption key instead of refusing startup/request processing makes credential ciphertext forgeable or decryptable under deployments that enable sync without configuring the key.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9 — P1 C100: `const state: IntegrationOAuthCallbackState = JSON.parse(req.query.state);` — OAuth state is accepted as unsigned, attacker-controlled JSON with no session nonce binding, enabling login-CSRF/credential planting by replaying an attacker-authorized callback into a victim's authenticated Cal.com session.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:35 — P1 C100: `members: { some: { userId: req.session?.user.id, accepted: true } }` — Any accepted team member, rather than a team administrator, is authorized to create shared team OAuth credentials and can install attacker-controlled integrations for the entire team.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — P1 C75: `const response = await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId: userId.toString(), appSlug }) })` — The credential-sync token endpoint is called with only guessable user/app identifiers and no authentication, forcing an exposed sync service to return OAuth access tokens to unauthenticated callers able to reproduce the request.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — P1 C75: `const appCredential = await prisma.credential.findFirst({` — The check-then-create sequence has no transaction or uniqueness-backed upsert, so concurrent sync deliveries can create duplicate user/app credentials and downstream `findFirst` readers can select an arbitrary version.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a race condition in the webhook handler. The code at lines 57-77 performs a findFirst to check if a credential exists, then either updates or creates based on the result. With concurrent webhook deliveries for the same userId/appId combination, two requests could both find no existing credential and both proceed to create, resulting in duplicate credentials. This is a real concurrency bug - there's no transaction wrapping the check-then-act sequence, and no unique constraint enforcement via upsert. The code should use a transaction or proper upsert with a unique constraint to prevent duplicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — P1 C75: `const response = await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, {` — The shared credential-sync dependency is invoked without an abort timeout, retry budget, or fallback, allowing one stalled endpoint to pin every expired-token calendar/video operation and exhaust shared request capacity.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the fetch call in refreshOAuthTokens.ts (lines 7-14) has no timeout, retry logic, or fallback mechanism. Looking at the diff, the function makes a POST request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT without any AbortController timeout or error handling beyond what the caller provides. If this endpoint is slow or unresponsive, it could block token refresh operations indefinitely. This is a real architectural concern for a production webhook endpoint that handles credential synchronization across multiple calendar/video integrations. The code as written could indeed cause operations to hang waiting for a stalled external endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:93 — P1 C100: `key: responseBody as unknown as Prisma.InputJsonValue,` — The sync endpoint is documented to return only an access token and expiry, yet this adapter replaces the whole credential with that partial response and therefore loses the refresh token and email required after the service is reconstructed.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts, I can see the refreshAccessToken function is modified to use refreshOAuthTokens. The code at line 93 (not shown in the diff but referenced) would be updating credentials with responseBody. The finding claims that when using the sync endpoint, only access_token and expiry are returned, which would overwrite and lose the refresh_token. Looking at refreshOAuthTokens in the diff, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT exists, it returns the response from that endpoint directly. The parseRefreshTokenResponse function (used in other adapters but NOT in office365video) has logic to handle missing refresh_token by setting a placeholder. However, office365video doesn't use parseRefreshTokenResponse - it directly uses the responseBody. If the sync endpoint returns only access_token and expiry (as documented), and this replaces the entire credential key, the refresh_token would indeed be lost. This is a real consistency issue where office365video wasn't updated to use parseRefreshTokenResponse like the other calendar services were.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at parseRefreshTokenResponse in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, it returns `refreshTokenResponse` which is the result of `safeParse()` - this is indeed a Zod SafeParseResult object with `{success, data, error}` structure, not the parsed data itself. In GoogleCalendarService.ts line 97, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` assigns this envelope object to `key`, which is then used in `data: { key }` for the credential update. This would store `{success: true, data: {...}}` instead of the actual credential data, breaking subsequent token access. This is a real bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — P1 C100: `if (req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET)` — When `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset, a request with the header omitted compares `undefined` to `undefined` and bypasses authentication, allowing arbitrary users' stored OAuth credentials to be overwritten.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 22-27, the authentication check compares `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-webhook-secret']` to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set (undefined or empty string), and a request comes in without that header, the comparison would be `undefined !== undefined` which is false, meaning the check passes and authentication is bypassed. This is a real security vulnerability - when the secret is not configured, any request without the header would pass authentication and could overwrite user credentials via the webhook endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — P1 C75: `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` — Falling back to a public empty encryption key instead of refusing startup/request processing makes credential ciphertext forgeable or decryptable under deployments that enable sync without configuring the key.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a security issue. In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts line 57, the code uses `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")`. If APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true but CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set, the code falls back to an empty string as the encryption key. This would allow an attacker to encrypt credentials with an empty key and have them accepted by the system. The code should validate that the encryption key is properly configured before attempting decryption, rather than silently falling back to an insecure default.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — P1 C75: `const response = await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId: userId.toString(), appSlug }) })` — The credential-sync token endpoint is called with only guessable user/app identifiers and no authentication, forcing an exposed sync service to return OAuth access tokens to unauthenticated callers able to reproduce the request.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for refreshOAuthTokens.ts, the function makes a fetch call to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with only userId and appSlug in the body, with no authentication headers or secrets. However, this is an OUTBOUND call from Cal.com to an external credential sync service (the self-hoster's application), not an inbound webhook. The security model here is that the self-hoster controls both Cal.com and the sync endpoint, so they're responsible for securing their own endpoint. The inbound webhook (app-credential.ts) does have authentication via CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header verification. The finding mischaracterizes this as an exposed endpoint that returns tokens to unauthenticated callers - but this is Cal.com calling OUT to a service the self-hoster controls, not exposing an endpoint. The self-hoster would configure their own endpoint's security.
